issues.title: Find a better name for the scheme
issues.author: kkohbrok
issues.body: So far we've called the scheme subgroups and virtual clients. The former clashes with RFC9420 ("Subgroup branching") and the latter is quite abstract and a bit too technical. Other options include "Multi-client" or "Multi-device", but that may be a bit generic, as there are other ways to use MLS with multiple clients/devices.

comments.author: Bren2010
comments.body: I actually really like the name virtual clients!

issues.title: Adopt reuse guard approach
issues.author: kkohbrok
issues.body:
Prior to adoption, we agreed that we wanted to switch to an approach where the reuse of nonces is prevented by the reuse guard. Adopting that approach also means that the number of emulating clients is limited.

The draft needs to be adapted to reflect that.

issues.title: Truncate PPRF input and nodes to 32 bytes for larger hash functions?
issues.author: kkohbrok
issues.body: The PPRF is already quite large with 32 bytes per node. Ciphersuites with larger hash function outputs unnecessarily make it even larger.

comments.author: kkohbrok
comments.body: This was solved by the switch to a SecretTree-style PPRF with a tree size corresponding to the RatchetTree of the emulation group.

issues.title: What are generation IDs?
issues.author: Bren2010
issues.body:
I'm confused about the purpose of this feature. It requires passing the group ID, epoch, generation, and ratchet type into a PRF with a secret key. But everything going into the PRF (except the secret key) is all public information. So what purpose does the PRF serve?

/cc @kkohbrok

comments.author: kkohbrok
comments.body:
TL;DR: It's to allow the DS to avoid storing the actual generation because that leaks activity metadata in the state-snapshot adversary model.

The DS has to persist some sort of information to detect duplicate use of individual ratchet generations of any virtual client. The emulator client sending a private message through a virtual client could just send the actual ratchet generation, but that would leak the number of messages sent by the virtual client in that particular epoch. Using pseudorandom generation IDs prevents that.

Of course the DS can always observe and count the number of messages. What this is trying to prevent is leakage in the threat model where an adversary only has access to state snapshots, but doesn't otherwise have visibility into network traffic.

comments.author: Bren2010
comments.body: Thanks! I will take a stab at writing up more context for this feature.

issues.title: Variant B resync removes every existing emulator client
issues.author: MarkAtwood
issues.body:
Variant B (L1059-1065, L1345-1348) joins with an external Commit that evicts the virtual client's prior leaf by a resync Remove. Every existing emulator client is that leaf, so under RFC 9420 §12.4.2 each concludes it was removed and drops the group. L853-855 says to process the Commit "like any other handshake message", and L637-640 covers only `external_init_secret`; nothing keeps them in.

Suggest: an emulator client processing an external Commit whose resync Remove targets the virtual client's leaf, and whose new LeafNode carries a valid DerivationInfo from its emulation group, does not treat itself as removed. It moves to the new leaf index and re-derives the leaf and path private keys from the DerivationInfo.

Found auditing -01 for mimid. Lines are draft-ietf-mls-virtual-clients.md at 65e960d.

issues.title: state_transfer: joiner can't compute interim_transcript_hash
issues.author: MarkAtwood
issues.body:
For Variant A, the transferred secrets (L1208-1223) plus "the RatchetTree and the GroupContext from an application-defined source" (L1057-1058) don't give the joining emulator client the previous Commit's `confirmation_tag` or the `interim_transcript_hash`. RFC 9420 §8.2 has new members compute it from the GroupInfo's `confirmation_tag`; the GroupContext alone isn't enough, so the joiner can't compute the next epoch's `confirmed_transcript_hash`.

Suggest adding `interim_transcript_hash` (or the last `confirmation_tag`) to the `state_transfer` case, or saying the application-defined source is a GroupInfo.

Found auditing -01 for mimid. Lines are draft-ietf-mls-virtual-clients.md at 65e960d.

issues.title: Privacy Considerations: key_package_upload exposes KeyPackageRefs to the emulation DS
issues.author: MarkAtwood
issues.body:
Virtual client actions travel as SafeAAD (L720-723), which is cleartext even in a PrivateMessage. A `key_package_upload` action therefore shows the emulation group's DS each `key_package_ref`, the `epoch_id` and the uploader's leaf, linking the virtual client's published KeyPackages to the emulation group and to one emulator client. The residual-metadata list (L1530-1556) doesn't include it.

Suggest adding it to that list, and optionally noting an encrypted alternative (e.g. an AppEphemeral proposal sent in a PrivateMessage, extensions-10 §4.8) for deployments that care.

Found reviewing -01 for mimid. Lines are draft-ietf-mls-virtual-clients.md at 65e960d.

issues.title: Check re-derived LeafNode and UpdatePath keys against the received ones
issues.author: MarkAtwood
issues.body:
L623-635 has emulator clients re-derive the key material of a received LeafNode and UpdatePath, but nothing requires comparing the derived public keys with the received `encryption_key` and UpdatePath keys, and nothing says what to do on an unknown `epoch_id`, a DerivationInfo that fails to decrypt, a deleted generation, or a mismatch. A faulty emulator client can install a leaf whose private keys the others silently get wrong.

Suggest requiring that comparison, and stating the action for each failure (e.g. reject the Commit, or mark the virtual client's state for resync).

Found reviewing -01 for mimid. Lines are draft-ietf-mls-virtual-clients.md at 65e960d.

issues.title: DerivationInfo key/nonce context: with or without the length prefix?
issues.author: MarkAtwood
issues.body:
L583-584 says the AEAD key and nonce use "the serialized `encryption_key` field of the LeafNode" as context, but the formula at L589-592 passes `encryption_key`. Since HPKEPublicKey is `opaque<V>`, "serialized field" suggests including the length prefix while the formula reads as the raw key bytes. Implementations that differ derive different keys and can't decrypt each other's DerivationInfo.

Suggest stating the exact bytes, e.g. "the TLS-serialized HPKEPublicKey, including its length prefix" (or the raw key bytes), and matching the formula to it.

Found reviewing -01 for mimid. Lines are draft-ietf-mls-virtual-clients.md at 65e960d.

issues.title: SecretTreeRatchetState can't carry retained skipped-generation secrets
issues.author: MarkAtwood
issues.body:
L256-262 requires retaining secrets for skipped operation-ratchet generations, and RFC 9420 allows the same for out-of-order application/handshake messages. But SecretTreeRatchetState (L1151-1164) holds only one `generation` and `next_secret`, while L1258-1261 says the transfer "MUST contain exactly the retained secrets needed to continue the Secret Tree deletion schedule". Skipped message-ratchet secrets have no place to go, and it's unclear whether RetainedOperationSecret (L1244-1247, "generation has been deleted") is meant to hold skipped operation secrets.

Suggest adding a per-ratchet list of retained (generation, secret) entries, or saying explicitly that skipped-generation state isn't transferred and relaxing the MUST.

Found reviewing -01 for mimid. Lines are draft-ietf-mls-virtual-clients.md at 65e960d.

issues.title: direct_path_private_keys can't express nodes whose key isn't held
issues.author: MarkAtwood
issues.body:
L1336-1340 defines `direct_path_private_keys` positionally: one HPKE private key per non-blank node in the filtered direct path, in order. Under RFC 9420, a leaf in a parent's `unmerged_leaves` doesn't hold that parent's private key, so where the virtual client is unmerged at some ancestor the provisioning emulator client has nothing to put in that slot, and every later key lines up with the wrong node.

Suggest giving each entry an explicit `node_index`, or stating that nodes where the virtual client is unmerged are omitted and how the receiver accounts for them.

Found reviewing -01 for mimid. Lines are draft-ietf-mls-virtual-clients.md at 65e960d.

issues.title: Say emulator clients accept PrivateMessages from their own leaf index
issues.author: MarkAtwood
issues.body:
L187-189 says a virtual client's PrivateMessage "can be decrypted by all emulator clients except the one that sent it", but those messages carry the virtual client's own leaf index as sender, which typical RFC 9420 implementations reject as their own message. Nothing says emulator clients MUST accept them, or that decrypting one at generation g advances the shared ratchet so later sends start at g+1 (which also reduces the collisions handled in L956-975).

Suggest one or two sentences to that effect in the Delivery Service section.

Found reviewing -01 for mimid. Lines are draft-ietf-mls-virtual-clients.md at 65e960d.

pulls.title: flesh out emulation client onboarding procedure
pulls.author: kkohbrok
pulls.body: (This PR is based #10.)

comments.body: Why does the joining emulator client have to send its own commit? Would be preferable for it not to
I think there's supposed to be a new header here separating trade-offs from the protocol definitions

Good point. I initially thought it would be easier for the adder to provide the new client only with the group state necessary to create a commit (upon which it could derive the remaining secrets in the new epoch). But it turns out the new client needs pretty much all possible secrets to do that. So you're right, it's not necessary to do a commit at that point.

If the new client doesn't update, we may run into trouble regarding the `reuse_guard` computation.

Both the number of emulator clients in a group and their leaf index go into the compuation of the `reuse_guard`. If we allow those two to change while the higher-level epoch stays the same, we run the risk of nonce collisions.

Consider the following scenario:

- There are two emulator clients (1 and 2) emulating a virtual client in group X
- Emulator client 2 sends a message in group X at ratchet generation 0 (which emulator client 1 never receives)
- Emulator client 1 removes emulator client 2
- Emulator client 1 adds emulator client 3 and transfers all of its group state
- Emulator client 3 now occupies the same leaf index as previously emulator client 2
- Emulator client 3 now sends a message into group X at ratchet generation 0

At the time emulator client 2 and emulator client 3 send their messages, they use the same `prp_key`, the emulator group is the same size and they occupy the same leaf index in the emulator group. The security of the message thus rests entirely on how random `x` really is.

All in all, I think it's safer if we mandate that the new client doesn't send any messages in groups until the virtual client has been updated in that group.

Since the reuse_guard computation is essentially bound to a certain configuration of the emulator group, maybe it makes sense to derive it once per emulation group epoch and then use it across all higher-level groups that use secrets derived from that epoch. That would make bookkeeping easier for implementations.

> Emulator client 1 removes emulator client 2

This step would require rotating the leaf in the supergroup, which would change the computation of the reuse_guard.

I could still see this being an issue though if we have emulator 1 and 2 in an emulation group, and then emulator 2 adds emulator 3. Because emulator 2 and 3 will be generating x's that are = 1 or 2 mod 3, while emulator 1 will be generating x's that are = 0 mod 2 until it learns about emulator 3.

Saying that a supergroup's LeafNode needs to be from the most recent emulator group epoch before you send a message seems like a good solution, yes.

> I went over it and it makes a lot of sense.

> Just leaving a note, no strong opinions: Have you considered a separate ratchet for each operation type? This assumes a fixed set of operation types. On the other hand, it may optimize storage. Three small points from reviewing -01 for mimid, left out of #53 because this PR rewrites the text they touch:

I believe this would violate the MUST of [9420's deletion schedule](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9420.html#name-deletion-schedule).

> It is important to delete all security-sensitive values as soon as they are consumed. A sensitive value S is said to be consumed if:
>
>   - S was used to encrypt or (successfully) decrypt a message, or a key, nonce, or secret derived from S has been consumed. (This goes for values derived via DeriveSecret as well as ExpandWithLabel.)
>
>Here S may be the init_secret, commit_secret, epoch_secret, or encryption_secret as well as any secret in a secret tree or one of the ratchets.
>
>As soon as a group member consumes a value, they MUST immediately delete (all representations of) that value.

That may be okay, but we should at least make that clear here.

pulls.title: Keep emulator clients in the group on resync external commit
pulls.author: MarkAtwood
pulls.body:
Fixes #36.

Adds a paragraph to "Externally joining groups": an emulator client processing a resync external Commit whose Remove targets the virtual client's leaf, and whose new LeafNode carries a DerivationInfo it can re-create, doesn't treat itself as removed; it moves to the new leaf index using the keys re-derived from the DerivationInfo.

pulls.title: Transfer interim_transcript_hash in state_transfer
pulls.author: MarkAtwood
pulls.body:
Fixes #37.

Adds `interim_transcript_hash` to the `state_transfer` case, with a bullet on why the joiner needs it: the GroupContext gives only the confirmed transcript hash, and RFC 9420 §8.2 needs the last `confirmation_tag` for the interim one. Requiring the application-defined source to be a GroupInfo would also work.

pulls.title: Note key_package_upload metadata exposed to the DS
pulls.author: MarkAtwood
pulls.body:
Fixes #38.

Adds a residual-metadata bullet: a `key_package_upload` action travels in cleartext SafeAAD, so the emulation group's DS sees each KeyPackageRef, the `epoch_id` and the uploader's leaf. Names an encrypted alternative, an AppEphemeral proposal in a Commit sent as a PrivateMessage.

pulls.title: Require checking re-derived virtual client keys
pulls.author: MarkAtwood
pulls.body:
Fixes #39.

Emulator clients MUST compare the re-derived public keys with the received LeafNode and UpdatePathNode keys, and reject the carrying message on a mismatch, unknown `epoch_id`, DerivationInfo that won't decrypt, or a deleted generation with nothing retained. Rejecting can leave that client out of step with a group that accepted the Commit; marking the virtual client's state for resync is the alternative.

pulls.title: Specify DerivationInfo key and nonce context bytes
pulls.author: MarkAtwood
pulls.body:
Fixes #40.

The DerivationInfo key/nonce context is now `serialized_encryption_key`, defined as the TLS-serialized HPKEPublicKey including its length prefix, and the formula uses that name. Raw key bytes would also work if you prefer.

pulls.title: Carry retained skipped generations in ratchet state
pulls.author: MarkAtwood
pulls.body:
Fixes #41.

Adds `retained_generations` to SecretTreeRatchetState so the "exactly the retained secrets" MUST can be met. Application/handshake entries hold the AEAD key and nonce (what RFC 9420 §9.2 keeps for skipped generations, so the deletion schedule is unchanged); operation entries hold the generation secret, since `operation_context` isn't known until the operation arrives. The alternative is to say skipped state isn't transferred and relax the MUST.

pulls.title: Index direct_path_private_keys by node_index
pulls.author: MarkAtwood
pulls.body:
Fixes #42.

Each `direct_path_private_keys` entry is now a DirectPathPrivateKey with an explicit `node_index`, and nodes where the virtual client's leaf is unmerged get no entry, so a missing key can't shift later keys onto the wrong nodes.

pulls.title: Accept PrivateMessages from the virtual client's leaf
pulls.author: MarkAtwood
pulls.body:
Fixes #43.

The Delivery Service section now says emulator clients MUST accept PrivateMessages from the virtual client's own leaf, which some RFC 9420 implementations reject as their own, and that decrypting one at generation g moves the shared ratchet past g, reducing the collisions handled in "Coordinating ratchet generations with the DS".

pulls.title: Low-severity fixes from an implementation review
pulls.author: MarkAtwood
pulls.body:
Low-severity fixes from reviewing -01 for mimid; each is independent, so drop any you don't want.

- HPKE key pairs from `init_key_secret` and `encryption_key_secret` were described only in prose, which lets emulator clients diverge (for example by adding RFC 9420's "node" step); the text now gives `KEM.DeriveKeyPair(...)` explicitly.
- Nothing said how `signature_key_secret` becomes a signing key, so emulator clients could derive different keys; an application that uses it now MUST specify that mapping for the target signature algorithm.
- No action was defined when `KeyPackageInfo.cipher_suite` and the KeyPackage's ciphersuite differ; the recipient now MUST discard that KeyPackageRef's material and MUST NOT process Welcomes addressed to it.
- The `external_secret` bullet said only that it lets others do external commits; it now says the joining emulator client needs it to derive `external_priv`/`external_pub`, process external Commits and publish GroupInfo for the epoch.
- Privacy Considerations did not mention that the fan-out DS learns which emulator clients stand behind a virtual client leaf and which one sent each message; added a residual-metadata bullet.
- The IANA registration asked for Recommended: Y, which RFC 9420 Section 17.1 reserves for Standards Action, and lacked the template's Reference field; it is now Recommended: N with Reference: RFC XXXX.

Not changed here: three more points touch text that #30 rewrites, so they're in a comment on #30 instead.
